name: Mandelbrot
miniText: How can repeatedly applying a simple complex map generate an intricate boundary? NetLogo Mandelbrot evaluates the iteration z squared plus c at grid locations, using moving agents to distribute computation and color patches according to their accumulated iterations and escape behavior. Mandelbrot [1] provides an original study of complex quadratic iteration, Milnor [2] supplies the mathematical dynamics, and Peitgen and colleagues [3] connect iterative maps with fractal geometry and computation. The model distinguishes bounded-looking orbits from escaping ones through finite work. A maximum iteration count cannot prove that a point belongs to the infinite mathematical set, especially near its boundary. Grid resolution and allocation of agent visits affect the developing image. The simulation illustrates numerical exploration of deterministic dynamics, rather than stochastic creation of the set or empirical evidence for a physical process.
